The oldest still-running university in the world is claimed by two competing traditions. Several high-credibility sources identify the University of Bologna, founded in 1088 in Italy, as the oldest continuously operating university in the world and the first degree-awarding institution in the medieval European model [d1,d2,d5]. In contrast, multiple sources—including one citing Guinness World Records—identify the University of Al Quaraouiyine (Al-Karaouine) in Fez, Morocco, founded in 859, as the oldest continuously operating, degree-granting university globally [d3,d4,d6,d7,d8,d9].
